title: Simple Receipt Printer
story: You and your friends set up a lemonade stand in the front yard. Business is booming! But handwriting receipts is slow and messy. Let's build a program that prints clean, professional receipts for every customer.
why: Printing formatted output with calculated totals is a real-world programming task used in stores, restaurants, and online shops every day.
analogy: A receipt printer is like a cash register — you tell it what was bought and how much, and it calculates the total for you.
expected_output:
=== LEMONADE STAND ===
Lemonade x2:
10
Cookies  x3:
12
--------------------
TOTAL:
22
Thank you!
try_it: Add a third item to your receipt (brownies? iced tea?) with its own quantity, price, and subtotal. Recalculate the grand total.
tips: Calculate subtotals BEFORE the grand total — `lemonade_total` and `cookie_total` feed into `grand_total`
Use separator lines (`-----`) to make your receipt easy to read — good formatting matters
Keep quantities and prices in separate variables so you can change prices without rewriting the whole program
common_mistakes: Forgetting to update the grand total when adding a new item — the total must include EVERY item's subtotal
Mixing up quantity and price — `lemonade` is how many, `lemonade_price` is how much each
